headline: Simultaneous Blasts Hit Four Corporate HQs — 'This Was a Message'
body:
At 8:14 AM on September 3rd, four coordinated explosions tore through the lobby atria of Axiom's North Spire complex, Sterling-Nakamura's financial tower, the Palladian administrative annex in The Circuit, and the Zheng-Dao regional logistics hub in Geartown — all within a window of ninety seconds. Preliminary forensic analysis confirms the devices were shaped charges placed at load-bearing structural points, suggesting professional installation during the prior 72 hours. All four buildings sustained significant structural damage; the Palladian annex has been condemned.

'This was not random,' said Commander Yeva Brantley-Okafor of the Meridian Joint Security Consortium. 'Four targets, four devices, one window. Someone planned this for months.' No group immediately claimed responsibility, though an anonymous broadcast on the Underground Signal aired within two hours reading a single statement: 'The Spires stand on our backs. Today they shook.' Authorities have not confirmed whether that message constitutes a claim of responsibility.

The Collective issued a public denial within hours, calling the attacks 'horrific and counterproductive to every value we hold.' Iron Lotus sources, speaking anonymously to this outlet, said the syndicate was 'as surprised as anyone.' The Graycloaks, characteristically, said nothing. Security analysts note the operational precision points to a group with access to corporate building schematics and the ability to insert personnel past multiple layers of biometric screening — a capability that narrows the suspect field considerably.

The combined death toll stands at 47, with 190 injured. Among the dead are nine synthetic employees of Sterling-Nakamura whose deaths are currently not classified as 'casualties' under Federal Remnant emergency statutes — a designation that has drawn sharp condemnation from synthetic rights advocates.
aftermath: A splinter cell calling itself Red Meridian claimed responsibility six weeks later via an encrypted broadcast; three of its alleged members were arrested by Arcturus Defense contractors in a raid on The Narrows that rights groups called 'a massacre in all but name.'
runner_relevance: The attacks immediately triggered a corporate security spending surge that flooded the runner market with protection contracts — every mid-tier executive in The Spires wanted a personal detail within 48 hours. Longer-term, the investigation itself became a contract economy: corporations hired runners to independently identify the attackers before law enforcement could, hoping to handle justice privately. Competing sabotage contracts also emerged, as at least two corponations suspected rivals of orchestrating the attacks and wanted evidence gathered or manufactured. Schematics retrieval — figuring out who accessed the building plans — became a high-value specialty contract paying upward of 80,000 quanta.
